title: Linux Internals
summary: Build miniature in-memory models of file descriptors, permission checks, signals and process trees, then combine them in a kernel-state checker.
description: Everything here is a small deterministic model in ordinary C: no real privileged system calls are made. You model descriptor tables with dup and close, the mode-bit permission rules including sticky and setuid, signal masks and delivery, and process trees with zombies and reparenting. The capstone combines them in a checker that validates a simulated kernel state. Each model shows only the rules it states; real Linux has many more details, and every lesson says which ones are left out.
outcomes: Explain and implement descriptor sharing through dup, dup2 and close.
Apply Unix permission rules including sticky directories and setuid execution.
Model signal masks and delivery, and process exit, zombies and reparenting.
Check a combined simulated kernel state against its invariants.
